Programme Outline

Awarded and developed by: Cardiff University, UK

The Bachelor of Science (Honours) in Computer Science with Security and Forensics programme aims to help students develop the knowledge and skills to safeguard digital systems. It covers the principles, tools and technologies needed to protect data and keep systems secure in an increasingly connected world.

This degree provides both the theoretical and practical knowledge required to become a part of the exciting and dynamic world of computer science which lies at the heart of almost all aspects of modern life, with a strong information security theme.

Learning Outcomes

  • Build a strong understanding of the concepts of risk and security in computing, along with secure coding techniques. 

  • Gain specialised knowledge of Security and Forensics in both theory and practical applications.

  • Develop transferable technical, analytical and professional skills, supported by a broad awareness of current technology trends, particularly in the field of computer security. 

Further Studies & Career Prospects

Business use of web applications and rising cases of cybercrime has fundamentally changed the nature of information security. As a concern for big business economies and consumers alike, graduates with an understanding of computer security and forensics are exceptionally valuable to many employers.

Graduates can objectively analyse problems and develop appropriate computational solutions. Their detailed understanding of technology computer security and digital forensics will make them suitable for a range of professional careers and sought-after by employers such as Cybersecurity Analyst, Penetration Tester (Ethical Hacker), Digital Forensics Investigator, Information Security Officer, Data Protection Specialist, Network Security Administrator. 

Why study at SIM x Cardiff University

Cardiff University's School of Computer Science and Informatics is accredited by the British Computer Society for Chartered IT Professional (CITP)

Cardiff University is ranked 22nd in the UK (The Complete University Guide 2026)
12th best UK university for employability (Times Higher Education 2026)
A member of the prestigious Russell Group of 24 UK research-intensive universities

Curriculum

Structure

  • Programme is mainly delivered face-to-face, in block teaching basis where lectures are conducted by Cardiff University teaching faculty, complemented by tutorials or lab work supported by local practitioners or academics.
  • View a list of lecturers’ teaching modules
  • Average teacher-student ratio: 1:100
  • Weekly schedule: Between Monday and Friday at three or six hours per session. Saturday classes may occasionally be scheduled if required.
  • Class timing: 8.30am / 12.00pm / 3.30pm, held on SIM campus unless otherwise stated
  • Minimum class size to commence: 30 students
  • If the class fails to commence due to low take-up rate, applicants will be informed within one month before programme commencement with the refund of application fee.

Show more Show less

Assessment & Attendance

  • There will be varied assessments which may include: 
    • Assignments 
    • Presentations 
    • Online Discussions 
    • Written Examinations
    • Projects 
  • Attendance requirement:
    • Local students – 75%
    • International students – 90%

Requirements to Graduate

  • To attain the Bachelor of Science (Honours) in Computer Science with Security and Forensics, students must complete all the requirements of the programme in strict compliance with the schedules and timelines defined for the cohort in which the student is enrolled or deferred. 
  • The awarded degree and degree certificate, is the same as that awarded in the UK, i.e. Bachelor of Science (Honours) in Computer Science with Security and Forensics. The word "Top-up" will not be reflected. 

Modules

The modules offered are pre-determined by the University. 

  • Human Computer Interaction (10 credits)
  • Internet of Things (10 credits)
  • Database Systems (10 credits)
  • Enhancing your Employability* (10 credits) 
  • Secure Communication Networks (10 credits)
  • Group Project* (20 credits)
  • Object Orientation, Algorithms and Data Structures (20 credits)
  • Data Processing and Visualisation (10 credits)
  • Informatics (10 credits)
  • Introduction to the Theory of Computation (10 credits)

  • Emerging Technologies (20 credits)
  • One Semester Individual Project^ (40 credits)
  • Artificial Intelligence (20 credits) 
  • Security (10 credits)
  • Forensics (10 credits) 
  • Large-Scale Databases (20 credits)

 

 

View list of modules and descriptions

Note:

  • *Taught and supervised by local lecturers.
  • **For BSc (Hons) in Computer Science with Security and Forensics, students are not required to take any optional modules as the core modules have fulfilled the 120-credit requirement for Year 3.
  • ^Includes online sessions with assigned supervisor from Cardiff faculty.
  • The modules listed here may occasionally be subject to change to ensure consistency with the UK programme. In such a scenario, you will be informed of any changes. 
  • Students are required to own a laptop equipped with at least Microsoft Windows 10 or Apple MacOS Catalina (10.15) and 8GB RAM (recommended).

Admission Criteria

Accepted Entry Qualifications

  • SIM Diploma in Information Technology; or 
  • Relevant Information Technology diplomas from local polytechnics 

All other qualifications shall be considered on a case-by-case basis and may be subject to interview. 

English Language Requirements

  • Minimum C6 pass in English as First Language at GCE 'O' Level; or 
  • IELTS score of 6.5 overall with minimum of 5.5 in each subskill; or 
  • TOEFL score of 90 overall with a minimum of 17 for writing, 17 for listening, 18 for reading, and 20 for speaking; or 
  • Pearson Test of English (Academic): At least 69 overall with a minimum of 59 in all communicative skills; or 
  • Successful completion of Part 2 of SIM Pre-Sessional English course (PSEC); or 
  • Successful completion of a recognised approved Diploma, where the language of instruction was English; or 
  • Equivalent 

Pre-sessional English Course (If Required)

Developed and awarded by SIM, Singapore.

Applicants who have not reached the required IELTS English Language proficiency level or equivalent shall have to complete and pass a Pre-Sessional English Course before progressing to any of the BSc programmes.

This full-time course aims to improve all four Academic English Language skills in Speaking, Listening, Reading and Writing to the required proficiency level for entry to the respective BSc programmes. 

A certificate of completion will be awarded upon successful passing of Part Two of the Pre-sessional English Course.

There will not be any refund or recourse should students fail to complete the course within the course duration.



* The PSEC is not open for direct application. The selection into the course is based upon recommendations by the Admission Committee (AC) for those who have applied to the respective BSc Programmes. 
** Fees are inclusive of 9% GST and are payable in full before each part of course commencement. Fees include online course materials.


Structure

  • Mode of delivery: Lessons will be delivered via blended learning with a combination of face-to-face lectures and e-learning components.
  • View module synopses
  • Class duration: Typically 6 hours on weekdays. Some lessons may also take place on Saturdays if required.
  • Assessments: Continuous assessments include in-class tests, individual / group assignments, online quizzes etc. There are no re-assessments.
  • Average teacher-student ratio – 1:30
    View a list of lecturers’ teaching modules (PDF 66 KB)
  • Minimum class size to commence – 25
    If the class fails to commence due to low take-up rate, students will be informed at least 1 week before programme commencement with the refund of application fee.
  • Attendance requirement:
    • Local students – at least 75% rate
    • International students – at least 90% rate
  • Maximum candidature: 2 months. There will be no refund or recourse should students fail to complete the programme within the candidature period.
